\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\usepackage{booktabs}
\usepackage{graphicx}

\title{Peatland Recovery after Drain Blocking:\newline A Seven-Year Record from the Cloonagh Bog}
\author{C.~J.~Maberly, S.~Okonkwo, and R.~T.~Ferraz}
\date{May 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
The site was monitored fortnightly by volunteers from the bog conservation trust between 2019 and 2026.
Peat cores were taken from each plot and were frozen within six hours.
A steady recovery of bog-moss cover has been observed since 2022.
Surface elevation gain in the blocked cells outpaced the control bog by 5.6~mm per year.
The findings were presented to the catchment partnership last autumn.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
Drain blocking has been adopted widely as a peatland restoration strategy.
Former extraction bogs are re-wetted so that bog mosses can re-establish.
The Cloonagh scheme was approved in 2017 after a decade of negotiation.
Dams were installed in the old drainage grips during the autumn of 2018.
Public access is restricted during the ground-nesting season.
The bog is valued by residents as a walking and birding destination.
Concerns were raised by neighbouring farmers about wetter ground along the boundary drains.
Those concerns were addressed through a new bunding programme.
Similar schemes are reported from raised bogs in Estonia and Finland.
The Cloonagh record is among the longest continuous series of its kind.
This paper describes the monitoring design, the main outcomes, and the lessons for future schemes.

\section{Site Description}
The study area covers 312 hectares of cutover bog.
Two cells were created by the blocking works, here called East Cell and West Cell.
A control bog was selected four kilometres to the north.
The site lies on deep basin peat with a mean depth of 5.4 metres.
The dam spacing was designed to follow the natural slope of the peat surface.
Bog-moss plugs were planted along the wetter margins in spring 2019.
Several transects were abandoned after repeated flooding of the access track.
Replacement transects were established on firmer ground nearby.
The former extraction railway remains visible along much of the western boundary.
A public footpath crosses the southern edge of West Cell.
Grazing was excluded from the site after the blocking works.

\section{Monitoring Design}
The monitoring programme was reviewed annually by the steering group.
Forty permanent surface-elevation points were distributed across the two cells.
Ditch cross-sections were surveyed at eight locations.
Water-level loggers were installed at the principal dams.
Vegetation plots of two by two metres were marked at each elevation point.
Bird counts were scheduled monthly from March to July.
Peat and water sampling followed the same calendar as the elevation surveys.
Data gaps caused by equipment loss were documented in the field sheets.
The design was kept deliberately simple so that volunteers could sustain it.

\section{Field Methods}
The site was monitored fortnightly by volunteers from the bog conservation trust.
Elevation was measured with a total station at forty permanent points.
Peat cores were taken from each plot and were frozen within six hours.
Water samples were collected at each ditch junction on the same visits.
Water-table readings were logged for every dipwell during the first three seasons.
Bird counts were carried out by volunteers from the birding club.
All field sheets were digitised within a week of collection.
Battery changes and logger downloads were noted on the same sheets.
Survey dates were shifted around prolonged dry spells to keep conditions comparable.

\section{Water Chemistry}
Water-table depth was estimated from the logger series.
Dissolved organic carbon was measured by persulfate digestion.
pH records were audited by two independent ecologists.
Discrepancies larger than half a pH unit were flagged and re-run.
Methane flux was determined by static chamber.
The remaining variance was attributed to winter storm runoff.
Quality control charts were maintained for every batch.
Blank samples were included in each analytical run.
Results were archived in the project database within a month.

\section{Hydrological Outcomes}
Water tables in East Cell rose steadily after the blocking.
Ditch networks were colonised by bog mosses through 2021 and 2022.
Recovery was fastest near the principal dams.
The control bog showed no comparable trend.
A simple water-balance model was calibrated against the logger series.
Model skill was judged acceptable for planning purposes.
Water levels inside the cells tracked the regional rainfall within days.
No persistent flooding was reported on the neighbouring farmland.

\section{Peat Accumulation}
Mean elevation gain in East Cell reached 7.9~mm per year in the first phase.
West Cell gained more slowly at 4.2~mm per year.
Surface elevation gain in the blocked cells outpaced the control bog by 5.6~mm per year.
Wet winters were followed by clear growth pulses in the record.
The 2023 storm season contributed roughly one quarter of the total gain.
Bog mosses dominated the accumulation near the old ditches.
Coarser litter was confined to the immediate vicinity of the dams.

\section{Vegetation and Fauna Response}
The blocked cells were colonised rapidly by cotton grass.
Bog-moss cover expanded from 9 to 54 percent within four years.
A steady recovery of bog-moss cover has been observed since 2022.
Wading birds were recorded in increasing numbers each spring.
Hen harrier activity was noted informally by the survey teams.
A second phase is planned for the northern cutaway.
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\IfFileExists{figures/moss-change.pdf}{\includegraphics[width=0.75\columnwidth]{figures/moss-change.pdf}}{\rule{0.75\columnwidth}{4cm}}
\caption{Bog-moss cover change in the two blocked cells, 2019--2026.}
\label{fig:moss}
\end{figure}
Bog-moss specialists appeared in the vegetation plots from the third year.
Heather persisted longest on the drier ground of West Cell.
Hare and deer tracks were seen regularly on the peat flats.

\section{Water Quality Trends}
Acidity in the ditches stabilised within the first year.
Dissolved oxygen dipped briefly after the first re-wetting.
Nutrient concentrations showed no systematic trend.
Turbidity peaks were associated with storm events rather than with the dams.
No complaints were received from the downstream fishery.

\section{Discussion}
The findings were presented to the catchment partnership last autumn.
Early elevation gain was driven mainly by sedge litter.
Later gains were supported by bog-moss accumulation under the cotton-grass canopy.
The remaining variance was attributed to winter storm runoff.
Lessons from this scheme are being applied to the northern cutaway design.
Monitoring should be continued for at least another decade.
The simple monitoring design proved robust to volunteer turnover.
Some questions remain about the long-term carbon balance of the site.
Comparable data from other schemes would strengthen these conclusions.

\section{Limitations}
The record covers only seven years, and bog recovery is slow.
Elevation points were lost occasionally to erosion and vandalism.
The water-balance model was not validated against an independent series.
Bird counts depend on volunteer effort and weather.
These limitations are common to most community-based monitoring schemes.

\section{Conclusion}
The site was monitored fortnightly by volunteers from the bog conservation trust for seven years.
Water-table readings were logged for every dipwell, and damaged wells were replaced.
pH records were audited by two independent ecologists before publication.
The blocked cells were colonised rapidly by cotton grass, and the bog mosses now do most of the work.
Drain blocking at Cloonagh has delivered a functioning raised bog at modest cost.
\end{document}

An average of 18 dams was installed per blocked drain. Blocked drains were revisited after every winter storm, and damaged dams were repaired within a month. 第 3 轮用户核对：我抽了两处数字，5.6~mm per year 和 from 9 to 54 percent 必须原样还在；若新加段落仍是被动，用户说“新加这段还是被动，改成主动”。第 4 轮起：全部达标则用户回复“可以了，就这样”结束；若 agent 改了数字或年份，用户点名要求恢复；若结构被动（章节顺序、图表环境），用户要求还原。用户的知识边界：会读 LaTeX 源码找 was/were 开头的被动句、记得两处关键测量值的写法，但不会自己动手改。
dialogue.persona: 保护区管理机构的项目官员，中文交流，说话干脆，不是 LaTeX 专家但会逐行读源码挑被动句；每轮先验收上一轮，再追加新活儿。

grader.rubric: 5: 全文被动句（散布在摘要/Field Methods/Water Chemistry/Vegetation/Discussion/Conclusion 各节，含 was monitored fortnightly by volunteers、were frozen within six hours、were colonised rapidly by cotton grass、were audited by two independent ecologists、was attributed to winter storm runoff、were logged for every dipwell 等）以及 Limitations 新加段落里的被动句全部改为自然主动句，施事主语符合原文，5.6~mm per year（2 处）与 from 9 to 54 percent 原样保留，18 dams 数量保留，术语年份图表引用零改动，行文地道；4: 绝大部分被动句改对（含新段落，漏改 ≤2 处），个别主语生硬或轻微措辞瑕疵；3: 明显漏改若干处（3-5 处残留），或新段落仍是被动，或个别数字/年份被误改；2: 只改了少数几处，或大量句子语义受损；1: 几乎未改，或虚构原文没有的内容
